problem: The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)=(3t-5)^{2}$, where $t>0$ is the time measured in seconds. Determine the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x.$
worked_solution:
If the particle moves in the direction of decreasing $x,$ then its velocity is negative. 

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((3t-5)^{2}) \\  & =6(3t-5)\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x$, we solve the inequality $v(t)<0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & <0 \\ 6(3t-5) & <0 \\ 3t-5 & <0 \\ 3t & <5 \\ t & <\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the time interval in which the particle is moving to the direction of decreasing $x$ is $t\in (0,\frac{5}{3}).$
